bullets: A newsroom is a reliability system with a deadline — a framing that clarifies which tradeoffs matter most in journalism.
Trust is the only asset a public broadcaster actually owns; ignoring it forces rebuilding from scratch a year later.
The second-order effects of reliability failures are the part most people miss, since they compound beyond the initial incident.
Reliability tradeoffs crosscut everything in journalism, making it the central lens for evaluating editorial decisions.
The practical takeaway is to pick one idea from the discussion and run it for two weeks, with the rest being iteration.
